headline: Qualcomm beat by a penny and sinks ~9% premarket on a weak guide; AppLovin +20%, Arm -5%; ConocoPhillips, Airbnb and Cloudflare report today
top_call: Qualcomm beat by a penny and still got dumped: down about 9% premarket after phone chip sales fell 26% and the next-quarter guide came in light. AppLovin beat, guided way above and is up about 20%. Arm beat, guided in line, and is off about 5%. Plain-English explainers below.
backdrop: Nasdaq futures slipped Thursday as chip stocks stayed under pressure, while S&P 500 futures were little changed after Wednesday's post-midterm rally. Qualcomm fell about 9% to 10% premarket after missing smartphone-chip estimates, and at least eight brokerages cut their price targets, according to LSEG data. Yahoo Finance premarket quotes at 7:05 AM ET: Qualcomm $156.85 (-9.4%), AppLovin $326.00 (+20.0%), Arm $182.64 (-4.8%).

ai.headline: OpenAI pledges to pay the full cost of powering its own data centers, publish construction plans and skip NDAs with public officials, two days after voters rebuked data-center expansion
ai.why: The midterms sent AI a power bill. OpenAI is paying it up front before someone sends a bigger one.

ai.headline: OpenAI says an agent pipeline running an upcoming cyber model produced 948 working Linux root exploits plus candidate patches in one run, for $1.21 million in API credits ($1,279 per exploit)
ai.why: Bug hunting just got a price per unit. Great for defenders, nervy for anyone who still hasn't patched.

ai.headline: Meta acquires Conductor, the startup that runs teams of coding agents in parallel; terms not disclosed, and Conductor Cloud shuts down Nov 20
ai.why: The new arms race isn't the model, it's the dashboard where the models do your job. Meta just bought one.
